key_insight: Alterbute is a diffusion-based image-editing model that can change intrinsic object attributes (color, texture, material, shape) while preserving the object's perceived identity and the surrounding scene context.
problem_solved: Existing methods either use weak unsupervised priors that lose object identity or rely on restrictive supervision that prevents realistic intrinsic variation; Alterbute enables flexible, identity-preserving edits of an object's intrinsic properties within a scene.
method: Diffusion-based localized editing: apply a conditional diffusion model focused on the object region to produce realistic intrinsic attribute changes.
Relaxed training objective that decouples attribute modification from identity and context changes, enabling larger intrinsic variations without identity drift.
Identity- and context-aware conditioning (e.g., region masks and identity-preservation constraints) to keep object identity and scene coherence during edits.
impact: Provides practitioners a practical tool for fine-grained, controllable object editing useful for content creation, data augmentation, and improving robustness of perception systems by generating realistic intra-class variation while keeping identity intact.
visual_elements: Before/after triplets showing edits of color, texture, material, and shape for the same object to illustrate preserved identity.
Pipeline diagram: input image + object mask → Alterbute (relaxed objective + conditioning) → edited image, annotated with key components.
Metric chart: identity-preservation score vs. edit strength comparing Alterbute to prior methods.
Overlay visualization (masks/attention) showing localized areas the model modifies vs. areas kept unchanged to emphasize context preservation.
paper_title: Alterbute: Editing Intrinsic Attributes of Objects in Images
paper_authors: Tal Reiss, Daniel Winter, Matan Cohen, Alex Rav-Acha, Yael Pritch
